title: 6.10.4 Lab: The paddle
description: A paddle along the bottom that follows the mouse, or the arrow keys, and never leaves the screen. The canvas and the paddle are made for you.

steps.title: Follow the mouse
steps.instructions:
The starter makes the canvas (400 by 400) and the paddle: a white `'static'` sprite 80 wide (`PADDLE_W`) and 12 tall at y 370. `'static'` means it never falls and nothing pushes it; your code moves it, like Defender's ship in 5.9.5. A variable `control` says who steers, `'mouse'` or `'keys'`, and it starts as `'mouse'`. `draw()` calls `movePaddle()` every frame, and the words at the top show `control` and the paddle's x. Right now `movePaddle()` is empty, so the paddle sits still in the middle.

In `movePaddle()`, when `control` is `'mouse'`, set the paddle's x to the mouse's x (`mouse.x`, 6.7.3). Run it and move the mouse over the canvas: the paddle follows it left and right and stays on its row, because only x changes. Move the mouse to the far left: half the paddle goes off the screen. Step 3 fixes that.
hints: Only x is set. The y stays 370, so the paddle can only slide sideways.

steps.title: Or the arrow keys
steps.instructions: Some players would rather use the keys. Add a second `if`: when `control` is `'keys'`, the left arrow moves the paddle 6 pixels left and the right arrow 6 pixels right, `if (kb.pressing('left')) paddle.x -= 6;` and the same with `'right'` and `+= 6` (5.1.13). Use `kb.pressing`, not `kb.presses`: the paddle should keep moving while the key is held (6.3.3). To try it, change `'mouse'` to `'keys'` in the line `let control = 'mouse';` at the top, press Run, and hold the arrows. Then put it back to `'mouse'`. The last lab of this module lets the player choose.
hints: `if (control === 'keys') { ... }` goes around the two key lines.

steps.title: Stay on the screen
steps.instructions: The paddle's x is its centre (5.1.6), so its left end is half a paddle to the left of x. It is fully on the screen while `paddle.x` is at least `PADDLE_W / 2` (40) and at most `400 - PADDLE_W / 2` (360). After the mouse and key lines, add two more `if`s: if `paddle.x` is less than `PADDLE_W / 2`, set it to `PADDLE_W / 2`; if it is more than `400 - PADDLE_W / 2`, set it to that. Run it and push the mouse (or hold an arrow) all the way to each side. The words stop at `paddle x: 40` and `paddle x: 360`, and the whole paddle stays in view.
hints: These two lines go after the mouse and key lines, so they correct wherever the paddle was put this frame.

requirements.title: The paddle follows the mouse
requirements.description: When control is 'mouse', the paddle's x is set to the mouse's x every frame. Help: 6.10.2 (Reading: A ball you move yourself)

requirements.title: The arrow keys move it
requirements.description: When control is 'keys', kb.pressing('left') and kb.pressing('right') move the paddle's x by 6. Help: 6.10.2 (Reading: A ball you move yourself)

requirements.title: The paddle stays on the screen
requirements.description: If its x goes below half its width, or above 400 minus half its width, it is put back on the edge. Help: 6.10.2 (Reading: A ball you move yourself)
